datatype_sweep.clip_bar_note: WITHDRAWN 2026-10-05 (06b). As written this note argued the brief's cross-mesh CLIP bar from p300x2 numbers (0.308699 and 0.183873) that were measured on BASE-model output -- the adapter was never on the weights that rendered them -- and it used 0.183873 as evidence of CLIP's natural spread when that clip IS the defect (the content-free coastline prompt, which the fixed build re-takes at 0.3690). Re-derived on the fixed build at a canvas-, frame- and prompt-matched pair, the bar is MET, not missed: p150 ctlB marching band at 1344x768 x124 scores 0.3366 against p300x2's 0.3239 for the same prompt and seed, 0.013 apart and inside the 0.02 bar. The surviving p150-only observation stands on its own: CLIP's spread between adjacent working points of ONE identical configuration is large (p150 1344x768 NFE4: 0.341777 at 124 frames vs 0.297044 at 73), so a cross-mesh CLIP delta is still a weak instrument. The dtype question was and is settled on the SAME mesh at the SAME point (see rejected[]), plus stage 04's component PCC bars.

optimized_by: stage 06 (see artifacts/s06/results.json); the matrix[] rows are stage 05 measurements at the PRE-optimization tree and are left as recorded. p150's DEFAULT also changed working point here -- NFE 8 -> NFE 4 on a five-prompt paired tiebreak -- which is a separate thing from the optimization gain and is recorded as such in p150.choice_reason and p150.superseded_nfe8_point. datatype_sweep[] is likewise a stage-05 record: its p150_policy.profile is the storage winner, not the served profile -- see datatype_sweep.p150_policy.profile_note.

p150.choice_reason: NFE 4, on the tiebreak stage 06 finally ran. Stage 05 chose NFE 8 on a +0.0582 CLIP margin at ONE prompt while recording that CLIP's own spread between adjacent points of one identical configuration is ~0.045. Re-run PAIRED over five prompts at this exact point and seed: NFE 8 wins 3 of 5, mean delta +0.0106 with a per-prompt stdev of 0.0255 (sem 0.0114, paired t 0.93 -- not distinguishable from zero), and the entire margin is the one prompt the original decision was made on: excluding it the mean delta is -0.0004. The latency price for that unestablished effect was 38.9%. Counter-reading, stated rather than hidden: stage 05's literal rule was 'keep the higher NFE if the margin is >= 0.01' and the 5-prompt mean margin (+0.0106) technically still clears it -- but that rule reads a mean without its spread, which is the flaw that produced the wrong answer the first time. Reverting is one line and every number is in the stage-06 record (nfe_tiebreak). The 80.6 s here is worst-of-five warm samples measured AT this profile; it is a working-point change and NOT part of stage 06's 147.7 -> 134.2 s optimization gain, which was measured at the NFE 8 point this default has now left.

dit_dtype_policy.mm_fp32_dest_acc_en_scope: all four block matmuls: to_qkv and to_out via attention_kwargs, ff1 and ff2 via the block. The block's config also reaches adaln_proj, a fifth matmul, but precomputed_adaln is true here so that projection never exists on device.
dit_dtype_policy.why: bf4_ff, the only storage alternative measured, is not faster and costs CLIP (see rejected[]). The arithmetic is a separate axis and stage 06 measured it over all four block matmuls: fp32 destination accumulation off is 2.5% of a block and 1.6% of the e2e, with full-depth video PCC 0.9930 against bf8_weights_bf8_out's 0.9927 and audio 0.9799 against 0.9840 (bars 0.99/0.95). LoFi is 12.5% of a block but scores video 0.9892, under the 0.99 bar by 0.0008, and is not offered as a profile; LoFi with bf16_blocks=(0,-1) was tried and is WORSE, video 0.9858, so the escape hatch this class documents does not buy back the 0.0008 and LoFi is rejected at both configurations.

p150.frames_headroom_MEASURED: MEASURED, not extrapolated: 1344x768 x124 at NFE 4 on this served profile is 157.9 / 161.9 s over two prompts (worst 161.9), INSIDE the 180 s budget, 16/16 content checks and 0 critical on both, CLIP 0.3366 / 0.3260 -- for 5.2 s of video instead of 3.0. The earlier ~165 s arithmetic was right. artifacts/s06/controls/ctlB_p150_x124.json. It is still NOT taken as the default here: that is a SECOND working-point knob and stage 06 had already moved one (NFE 8 -> 4), so stage 07/09 owns the decision -- but it now owns a measurement instead of an estimate.

superseded_nfe8_point.why_kept: this is the point stage 06's OPTIMIZATION gain was measured at, and losing it would leave the 147.7 -> 134.2 s pair with nothing in this file to anchor it. It is no longer the default; the tiebreak moved the default to NFE 4.

tiebreak.content_checks: 16/16, 0 critical, on all ten tiebreak clips and all five served-profile clips

p300x2.choice_reason: chosen on latency and canvas; the quality fence this line used to carry is LIFTED -- see `quality`, re-taken 2026-10-05 on the build that fixed the on-device LoRA bind. Within budget. Stage 06 took the e2e from 75.5 s to 71.7 s here: the (1,4) preset has sp_axis 0 over a mesh of shape (1,4), so sp_factor is 1 and the ring-free windowed SDPA path applies on this mesh too -- but with 14 heads per device rather than p150's 56, and the chunk-size optimum moves with head count, so this mesh takes (512, 128) where p150 takes (384, 256). Measured at 14 heads at all three lengths this profile can serve: 19328 -11.8%, 22464 -4.2%, 37760 -4.8% against the 56-head pick. The CLIP comparison that used to close this paragraph (0.3344 against stage 05's 0.3087) is WITHDRAWN 2026-10-05: both numbers were measured on base-model output, so the pair says nothing about the chunk rule or anything else. The chunk rule's evidence is the per-length device measurement quoted above, which is unaffected. See `clip` / `clip_note` for the re-taken quality numbers.
p300x2.clip_note: RE-TAKEN 2026-10-05 (06b). The 0.3344 that stood here, and stage 05's 0.3087 it was compared with, were both BASE-model measurements -- the adapter was never on the weights that rendered them (artifacts/s06/results.json p300x2_quality_numbers_are_base_model). This is the mean over the five prompts in artifacts/s06/nfe/prompts.txt at seed 7, on the fixed build. No CLIP number measured on this profile before 2026-10-05 should be quoted.

dit_dtype_policy.why: the (1,4) preset asks for no quant profile: TP=4 divides the DiT to ~16.6 GB/chip and the measured default clears the 90 s budget, so there is nothing to buy by quantizing on latency. CORRECTED 2026-10-05 (06b): the stage-06 sentence that the served-point quality defect 'lives on this bf16 path' is WITHDRAWN. The defect was the on-device LoRA bind not surviving a weight page-in; it is fixed in the shared layer and this profile's quality is re-taken as good at bf16. bf8 appeared to cure it only because a quant profile also moves the adapter to the host fuse. Nothing about the dtype needs to change.

p300x2.e2e_note: WORST of five prompts on the fixed build (stage 06b), against stage 06's 71.7 s worst-of-two. The difference is the fix's one new per-request cost: re-applying the adapter on the DiT page-in re-uploads 208 rank-128 A/B pairs from host. It is invisible in phases_s -- denoising is unchanged (36.1 s on the coastline prompt against the no-adapter control's 35.9 s, so the merge still has no per-step cost) -- and shows up as wall-minus-phases going 17.6 s -> 20.1 s, flat across all five clips. Peak DRAM is unchanged AGAINST ctlG, which shows the same prompt-driven 19.94 -> 21.65 step, rather than constant: the re-merge adds no DRAM (lora_cache_capacity is 0, so the factors are freed per apply). The record carries the worst of the five, 21.65 -- see peak_dram_gib_note. Still inside the 90 s budget. Removable: LoRAMixin's A/B LRU exists for exactly this re-merge and would buy the 2.4 s back for about 0.5 GiB/device; not taken in 06b because it moves the memory profile this record was measured at.
p300x2.peak_dram_gib_note: WORST of the five prompts at this point, matching how e2e_s and phases_s are sampled in this block. The value here used to be 19.94, which is the MINIMUM of the same five. The 19.94 -> 21.65 step is reproducible and pre-existing -- stage 06's ctlC, ctlF and ctlG all show it on their second (blacksmith) clip -- and it is prompt-driven, not an effect of the LoRA page-in re-merge, which adds no DRAM at all (lora_cache_capacity is 0, so the A/B factors are freed per apply). Size stage 07/08 against 21.65.
p300x2.phases_s_source: s06b_p300x2_fixed_p0_1344x768x124, the worst-of-five run `e2e_s` reports, so the two are one sample. wall - sum(phases) = 20.2 s here; see e2e_note for what lives in that gap. The per-prompt spread in `denoising` (36.1-42.4 s across the five) is the padded packed length changing with the prompt's token count, the same spread stage 06's controls show.
p300x2.quality: RE-TAKEN 2026-10-05 (stage 06b) on the fixed build and now GOOD. The stage-06 defect was not a working-point problem at all: the on-device LoRA bind was inert across the DiT page-in this `coresident: False` preset performs before every denoise, so every clip ever recorded on this profile was BASE-model output. Fixed in tt_dit's shared LoRA layer (commit 'Keep a fuse-mode LoRA bound across a weight page-out'). Five prompts, seed 7, one build, warm, at this exact point: CLIP 0.3239 / 0.3589 / 0.3690 / 0.3218 / 0.3381, temporal motion 8.47 / 6.44 / 1.28 / 3.10 / 1.96. The motion collapse is gone (it was a 0.70-0.89 floor on 3 of 5), the content-free coastline clip is gone (CLIP 0.1867 -> 0.3690) and the dark blacksmith clip is back in p150's range (video mean 4.0 -> 11.1 against p150's 13.9). Cross-checked against stage 06's INDEPENDENT bf16 host-fuse control ctlF, a different code path to the same model, on its two prompts: coastline 0.3690/1.28/107.7 here against ctlF's 0.3647/1.239/108.5, blacksmith 0.3218/3.10/11.1 against 0.3227/2.529/10.4. artifacts/s06b/results.json.
p300x2.quality_fix_measured: SUPERSEDED 2026-10-05 by the real fix; kept only so the stage-06 reading is not silently deleted. The one-axis bisect that produced it was sound as measurement and wrong as diagnosis: ctlE's bf8 arm recovered the output because setting a quant profile ALSO switches the adapter onto the host-fuse path (`_lora_fuses_on_host`), not because bf16 arithmetic was the problem. ctlF held the dtype at bf16, forced the host fuse, and recovered everything too -- which already exonerated the dtype inside stage 06. There is no accuracy reason to quantize this mesh. See artifacts/s06b/results.json.
p300x2.quality_known_exception: 1 of the 5 clips fails exactly one critical prove_h3 check and it is NOT this profile's problem: 'a red fox trotting through fresh snow at dawn, crisp footsteps crunching' scores audio rms 0.0019 against prove_h3's absolute 0.002 floor. The SAME prompt and point run through the independent host-fuse path (MINIMAX_H3_FORCE_HOST_FUSE=1) gives 0.0018 and fails the same check, with CLIP 0.3598 against 0.3589 and motion 6.32 against 6.44 -- so the two adapter-application paths agree and the quiet audio is the prompt. It is also the quietest prompt of the five on p150 (rms 0.00500 at 73 frames, the lowest of its five), and this clip is 124 frames / 5.2 s of audio against p150's 73 / 3.0 s, so sparse footsteps spread over a longer clip land lower in RMS. Stage 07 owns the call: either prove_h3's audio floor is made duration-aware, or this prompt is expected to fail it on a 5 s clip. Nothing here says the model is wrong. artifacts/s06b/s06b_ctlH_fox_hostfuse.json.  UPDATED 2026-10-05 after a second review. A frame-count control was run (fox at 1344x768 x73 on this same profile: rms 0.00238, PASSES, with total audio energy essentially unchanged at 1.724e-05 against the 124-frame clip's 1.905e-05), so for THIS prompt the longer clip is the same audio diluted. Two things must not be over-read from that. First, it is a one-prompt result: on p150 the same 73 -> 124 change costs 16.6x of total audio energy on the marching-band prompt, so frame count is NOT generally energy-neutral and that effect is open (artifacts/s06b/results.json open_items). Second, the duration-MATCHED cross-mesh comparison (stage 06's ctlB, p150 at x124) shows no p300x2 audio deficit at all on the two prompts it covers -- p300x2 is louder on one and equal on the other -- so the p150/p300x2 gap on the fox clip is a one-prompt, one-length observation, not a profile property. The served profile ships with a known 1-in-5 failing content check on this prompt; stage 07 owns whether the floor or the prompt moves.
p300x2.within_budget_note: `within_budget` and `e2e_s` are latency facts and remain true. They say nothing about whether the clip is correct; see `quality`.

adaln_lever.status: MEASURED and NOT taken. Recorded here so stage 07 can decide with the numbers rather than re-run the arm.
adaln_lever.what: precomputed_adaln true on the (1,4) preset -- the AdaLN branch evaluated into host tables instead of resident on device. The (1,1)/p150 preset already serves it; on (1,4) TP=4 fits the resident branch, so it was never needed and never measured with the adapter applied until now.
adaln_lever.held_fixed: mesh 1x4, 1344x768 x124, NFE 4 (steps 5), 4step_v1.2_768p_bf16 @1.0, video shift 6 / audio shift 3, seed 7, text encoder on device, no quant profile, same build, same five prompts in the same order (artifacts/s06/nfe/prompts.txt), warm pass. The two prompts it shares with the 2-prompt first pass render bit-identical (video AND audio sha256), so the arm is deterministic.

motion.note: up on 4 of 5; the coastline clip 1.28 -> 2.68 is stage 06's original adaLN observation reproduced with the adapter genuinely applied. Corroborated by p150's served coastline clip at motion 3.48 and by three independent adapter-applied RESIDENT renders (ctlE 1.228, ctlF 1.240, device bind 1.280) agreeing the resident branch pins this prompt near 1.24.

clip.note: a wash: mean 0.3423 -> 0.3398, largest per-prompt move 0.0114 against the ~0.045 spread CLIP shows between adjacent points of one identical configuration.

in_favour.where_the_wall_win_actually_is: NOT in compute. step_s and the denoising phase are unchanged between the arms (10.57-10.59 s per step both ways); the whole 74.6 -> 67.3 s is wall-minus-phases, 20.0-20.2 s resident against 12.7-12.9 s precomputed. That is the same untimed weight page-in gap that fix_cost.removable says a capacity-1 A/B LRU would buy about 2.4 s back from, and that fix_cost.caveat_from_review says has uncharacterised run-to-run spread. The two savings overlap and must NOT be added.

audio_rms_falls_on_five_of_five.convention: prove_h3's own audio_rms for both arms: RMS over a 32 kHz STEREO AAC decode of the mp4. prove_h3.decode_audio passes ffmpeg -ac 2 and the RMS is taken over both channels, and this is the same number prove_h3's 0.002 floor check reads. CORRECTED 2026-10-05: this said 'mono'. It never was. No ratio or decision changes -- every number here is the same metric computed the same way -- but a downmix to one channel moves it, and by how much depends on the matrix -- which matters to anyone acting on quality_known_exception's stage-07 item about making the floor duration-aware. `ffmpeg -ac 1` SUMS at 1/sqrt(2) per channel and runs +14.8% to +37.5% higher across these ten clips; an arithmetic average (L+R)/2 runs exactly 1/sqrt(2) of that, i.e. BELOW the stereo value. On the one clip that fails the floor the three readings are 0.0018961 stereo (fails by 5%), 0.0021767 at -ac 1 (would pass) and 0.0015391 averaged (fails by 23%), so the convention decides the answer and must be stated with any downmix figure.

against_and_why_it_is_not_taken.it_pushes_the_one_failing_clip_further_u: the fox clip goes from 5% under prove_h3's absolute 0.002 floor (0.0019) to 38% under (0.0012).
against_and_why_it_is_not_taken.it_is_not_a_property_of_the_flag: the SAME axis on base-model weights moves audio the OTHER way. Quoted in audio_rms, the same metric and convention as the cost above, so the two sides of this argument are comparable: ctlG (resident) -> ctlD (precomputed) goes 0.0231892 -> 0.0279340 (+20.5%) on the coastline prompt and 0.0120094 -> 0.0213720 (+78.0%) on the blacksmith. (The same pair in audio abs max reads 0.1246 -> 0.1468 and 0.2420 -> 0.3072 -- same direction, weaker statement.) So the drop is not what host adaLN tables simply do; it is specific to this configuration and uncontrolled.
against_and_why_it_is_not_taken.it_weakens_the_cross_mesh_sentence_the_f: at the served resident setting the duration-matched p150-vs-p300x2 audio comparison reads +61% / +5% (p300x2 louder or equal). Re-derived on the precomputed arm it would read about +5.5% / -10.5%, i.e. marginal on one prompt and inverted on the other. UNIT (named here because the two sibling keys name theirs): these are TOTAL AUDIO ENERGY, mean(x^2) * duration over both channels of the .wav -- not the audio_rms the cost above uses. p150 ctlB 5.0630e-03 / 3.2632e-03 against resident 8.1610e-03 / 3.4140e-03 and precomputed 5.3430e-03 / 2.9205e-03.
against_and_why_it_is_not_taken.verdict: one-directional, arm-wide, on half of what this model outputs, with no control and no explanation. A ~20% audio amplitude cost is not bought by 9.8% wall and 6.16 GiB in the stage whose entire reason for existing is that a silent quality defect shipped under an adapter's name.

adaln_lever.what_would_close_it: An audio-branch control at the served setting: the audio decode path with adaLN precomputed vs resident on identical latents, to separate 'the host adaLN table changes the audio modulation' from 'the two arms sample different trajectories'. If the drop is explained or shown benign, the lever is worth taking -- it is cheaper and smaller and better on motion. Owner: stage 07.
